body.text: In short:
Israel has honoured five of its citizens who prevented a passenger plane from crashing with heroism awards.
One pilot told the ABC it was a miracle people survived.
What's next?
An Israeli minister has called for the co-pilot who stabbed the plane's captain in midair to be extradited to his country for "a life of hell".
Israel has honoured five of its citizens who helped fight off a pilot who attempted to crash a passenger plane as it flew to Israel with heroism awards.

Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai was scheduled to land in Tel Aviv on Wednesday, but was diverted and landed in Saudi Arabia after one pilot stabbed the other in the cockpit and "apparently tried to crash the plane", according to Israel's prime minister.
But passengers and crew aboard the Boeing 737 Max 8 were able to foil the co-pilot's attempt to crash the jet and managed to safely land it after it plummeted thousands of metres in a minute.
"You put yourselves at risk to save others and prevented a terrible disaster," Israel's President Isaac Herzog said in a statement.
"The whole world saw the beautiful and courageous face of Israeli society.
"I am proud of you, and I thank you on behalf of the state of Israel."
Among the Israelis to receive the Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism was Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber who seized control of the plane, helping save all 174 people on board.
Foreign Minister Penny Wong confirmed at least two Australians were on the plane and were safe, thanking the "heroes who thwarted the attack and helped bring the passengers to safety".
Mr Hayoun, still wearing a bloodied shirt, was personally greeted at Ben Gurion Airport by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who called him "a hero who has saved many lives".
Another award recipient, Asaf Rajuan, said it was an "extraordinary incident".
"We felt helpless, suspended in midair, and I didn't know who to turn to," he said.
"But it was all instinct: to survive, to save the family, the people, and the children."

Mr Herzog and Mr Netanyahu have also praised the plane's Indian pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar, who Israeli officials said managed to open the cockpit door to let passengers and crew save the plane after he was stabbed by the co-pilot.
Mr Machchhar is in a good health and recovering well in hospital, according to the the Indian embassy in the UAE.
"He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals," Mr Netanyahu said in a post on X.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called him a "hero".

"In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy," Mr Modi said.
Pilot says survival of passengers 'close to a miracle'
Pilot Gyorgy Peto, who is also a former aviation journalist, told the ABC the landing of this plane made "the landing on the Hudson like a walk in the park".
"Honestly the chances that this was survivable was pretty much close to zero," he told The World.
He said the aircraft was "close to breaking the speed of sound" when it descended so rapidly.
"There are a lot of small bits here that are close to a miracle, but this whole thing is just stunning in itself," Mr Peto said.
"Luck is a very important player in this whole equation."
He said the incident would inevitably bring changes to the aviation industry.
"The whole flying set-up, from a security point of view, was never planned that the pilots would attack each other," he said.
"I think there's a lot of changes coming, and a lot of uncomfortable changes, because of this."
Mr Peto said that should include better, more stringent background checks on pilots.
Minister calls for 'terrorist' pilot to face 'life of hell' in Israel
Mr Netanyahu claimed the flydubai co-pilot involved in the midair incident, identified as an Omani national, had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".

But the United Arab Emirates has started its own investigations seeking to establish the circumstances and motives, and determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction", according to UAE state news agency.
Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said the co-pilot, along with the pilot, had been transferred from the kingdom to the United Arab Emirates on Thursday, local time.

"After their health improved and the medical team cleared them, they left the Kingdom heading to Abu Dhabi on Thursday morning, accompanied by the Emirati security team," the ministry said in a statement, adding that the initial investigation showed the co-pilot attacked the captain.
Israeli Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir said he wanted the pilot extradited to Israel.
"I will demand in the cabinet to extradite the terrorist pilot who wanted to harm hundreds of innocent Israelis to Israel," he wrote on X.
"Here, he will encounter my policy in the prisons very well on his own flesh, a life of hell awaits him here!"
ABC/AFP/Reuters
